idea.title: Claude Code leaks: what the numbers say
idea.topic: Claude Code privacy/security blow‑ups (email leakage, password exposure, Goldman Sachs pull‑back)
idea.short_title: Claude Code leaks: what the numbers say
idea.the_news: Claude Code was found to send users’ email addresses to third‑party sites and expose passwords in public repos, prompting Goldman Sachs to pull the tool.
idea.what_you_do: I scraped the top 20 Hacker News comments on the three leak threads, counted unique email mentions and password patterns, and measured how quickly the leaks propagated to public forks.
idea.post_shows: A quick audit that quantifies the exposure and shows the speed at which agentic LLMs can leak data in production.
idea.why_hired: Shows I can audit risky LLM integrations fast and spot production‑ready safety gaps.
hook_options: Claude Code sent 1,600+ HN points of data leaks—here’s the 5‑minute audit I ran to count every exposed email.
Goldman Sachs quit Claude Code. I traced the leak chain in under 2 hours—what a production team must know.

option.what_it_is: A tiny CLI (`cc‑shield`) that sits between your code and Claude Code. It strips PII (emails, passwords) from the prompt, injects a sandbox token, and logs every outbound request. The wrapper then calls Claude Code via its npm package to get the suggestion and returns it to the user.
option.what_you_show: A 45‑second screen‑recording: a vulnerable Python script with a hard‑coded password is fixed by `cc‑shield` – the password never appears in Claude Code’s response nor in any network trace (verified with Wireshark). The repo is public: https://github.com/nirajb/cc‑shield
option.why_hired: Shows I can ship production‑grade AI tooling that protects user data, a must‑have skill for any early‑stage AI product.
option.twist: Most leak‑explanations just point out the problem; this demo proves a practical, reusable fix that any startup can drop into its pipeline.
option.title: Demo‑app
option.your_edge: Built a privacy guard in <45 min, tested with real PII, and open‑sourced it.
option.why_hiring_cares: Security‑first engineering, rapid prototyping, and open‑source impact.
option.who_it_impresses: Founders needing fast, safe AI‑assisted dev tools.
option.stand_out: Turns a headline‑making flaw into a product feature you can ship tomorrow.
option.difficulty_why: Uses existing npm package, simple stream processing, no heavy compute.
steps_preview: Write `cc‑shield.js` to read stdin, regex‑redact PII, call Claude Code, output result.
Add a Wireshark capture to prove no PII leaves the box.
option.risk: Running Claude Code still contacts Anthropic; the wrapper must be used in trusted environments.
option.hook: I built a privacy‑guard CLI around Claude Code that stops email/password leaks – {{result}}.

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.

**Learn more in the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)**.

## Data collection, usage, and retention
When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the `/bug` command.

## How we use your data
See our [data usage policies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage).
